objective: Rewrite backend/src/spotify/nowPlaying.ts's polling schedule (BACKLOG.md #24, see analysis/24-event-scheduled-now-playing-poll.md for the full design) to replace the current flat setInterval(4000)-based startNowPlayingPoller with event-scheduled polling driven by three triggers: (1) an exported function that lets a caller (e.g. a future playback-route handler in a follow-up task, NP1.2) request an immediate one-shot poll; (2) a scheduled one-shot poll timed around each currently-playing track's expected end (durationMs - progressMs + a small buffer, e.g. 500-1000ms) to catch Spotify auto-advancing to a new track without any explicit action; (3) a 15-second safety-net poll (SAFETY_INTERVAL_MS = 15000) that always fires if nothing else has polled more recently, to catch anything else (external/out-of-band playback changes via a device's own controls or another Spotify client, general drift) and to keep device-online/offline detection alive (it currently piggybacks on every poll's `device` field). At any point, the *next* scheduled poll should be whichever fires sooner: the end-of-track timer (if a track is currently playing) or the safety-net timer -- and each real poll result should reset/reschedule both timers based on the fresh state. When nothing is playing (isPlaying: false / no track), there is no end-of-track timer to schedule -- only the safety-net interval applies. The critical constraint: pollNowPlaying()'s own body (track-change detection via hasChanged(), play-history/leaderboard recording, lyrics lookup, device-status updates via updateDeviceStatusFromDeviceField/checkDeviceStatusFallback, and the isRateLimited() backoff check at the top) must NOT be changed at all -- this task is purely about changing what schedules calls to the existing, unmodified pollNowPlaying() function, not about changing what that function does once called.
non_goals: Do not modify pollNowPlaying()'s own internal logic (track-change detection, play-history/leaderboard recording, lyrics lookup, device-status updates, rate-limit backoff check) -- only the code that decides WHEN to call it.

Do not touch playback.ts, admin.ts, or any route file -- wiring the own-action fast-path trigger into playback.ts's pause/resume/skip/previous routes is NP1.2's job, a separate dependent task. This task only needs to EXPOSE a way for a future caller to trigger an immediate poll + reschedule (e.g. an exported function), not wire it into any route.
Do not touch queueSync.ts, device.ts, client.ts, or any other Spotify module.

Do not change the existing isRateLimited()/recordRateLimitFromResponse() rate-limit backoff mechanism -- it must continue to apply exactly as it does today, regardless of which trigger caused a given pollNowPlaying() call.

Do not implement the QUOTA_EXCEEDED-vs-rate-limit distinction from analysis/22-spotify-api-call-inventory.md's 'concrete follow-up' section -- that's a separate, not-yet-scoped task, unrelated to this one.
acceptance_criteria: startNowPlayingPoller no longer uses a flat setInterval(4000) firing on a fixed cadence -- it uses a scheduling mechanism (e.g. setTimeout chains) where the delay to the next poll is recomputed after each poll based on the current state.

When a poll result shows isPlaying: true with a known durationMs and progressMs, the next automatic poll is scheduled at min(remaining-time-until-track-end + a small buffer, SAFETY_INTERVAL_MS=15000) from that poll's completion -- i.e. whichever is sooner.
When a poll result shows nothing playing (isPlaying: false or no trackId), the next automatic poll is scheduled at SAFETY_INTERVAL_MS (15000ms) -- there's no track-end to schedule against.

An exported function (name and exact signature are the implementer's judgment call, but it must be usable by a future caller outside this file) exists that triggers an immediate one-shot poll and correctly cancels/reschedules any pending scheduled timer so there's no stale duplicate timer left running afterward, and no double-poll race.

pollNowPlaying()'s own function body is unchanged from before this task (verify via diff -- only add/change code around it, in startNowPlayingPoller and any new scheduling helpers, not inside pollNowPlaying itself).

The isRateLimited() check inside pollNowPlaying() continues to gate every poll call regardless of which of the three triggers caused it -- a poll that fires while rate-limited still returns early exactly as it does today, and the scheduling logic still schedules a next attempt afterward (doesn't get stuck).

stopNowPlayingPoller (or an equivalent) still cleanly stops all pending scheduled polls (both the safety-net timer and any pending end-of-track timer), leaving nothing running -- verify no timer leaks in tests (e.g. via vi.useFakeTimers()/vi.getTimerCount() or equivalent).

New/updated tests in nowPlaying.test.ts cover: (a) the scheduling picks the sooner of end-of-track-delay vs. the 15s safety interval correctly in both directions (a track ending in 3s schedules for ~3s+buffer, not 15s; a track with 60s remaining schedules for 15s, not 60s); (b) nothing-playing state uses the 15s safety interval; (c) the immediate-poll-trigger function correctly triggers a poll and reschedules without leaving a duplicate/stale timer; (d) stopping the poller cancels all pending timers.
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit and npx vitest run both pass clean.
